title: 30 October International Day of Action: Find Your Local Port Action (No Harbour for Genocide // Europe Palestine Network)
content:
A post shared by No Harbour For Genocide (@noharbour4genocide)

In nine days, on 30 October, dockworkers in more than 100 ports across Europe, Asia, Africa and America are taking action together, under the slogan: Dockworkers do not work for war. The unions call it one of the biggest coordinated workers’ actions the docks have ever seen.

Dockworkers who act without people at the gates will bear the brunt of the repression that follows, so stand with them.

We’ve built a tool to help you find the action nearest to you. Use it at the link in bio.

The map shows every port we can name so far, grouped by country, with times and meeting points added as unions confirm them. Check back before the 30th; the list is still growing.

It also tells you what passes through your port. We have documented 315 shipments of Elbit Systems components through 56 commercial ports and 3,400 shipments supplying US military bases through 67 ports. Where we have documented transfers from this database or the press for 2025-2026, the port’s entry says so.

Not near a port? Join a solidarity action in your city, push the Istanbul Declaration, share the poster. If you are a union member, dockworker, port worker or seafarer, use our template to write to your union. If you live in a port city, use our template letter to write to your port authority.

title: Dezionizing the University of California
content:
Sean Malloy and Ethnic Studies Council at UC

In September 2025, I wrote a guest post for Chris Newfield’s blog that highlighted the complicity of UC leadership and the Academic Senate in federal attacks on the university under the guise of combating antisemitism. In a follow-up guest post in May 2026, I identified Zionism as the driving force behind many of the external and internal threats to the UC and its faculty, staff, and students. Building on those earlier writings, I want to explore at some length what it would mean to “dezionize” the University of California. Anti-Zionism is not new and has existed since the creation of the Zionist political movement. Given the stakes of the current moment, however, it is not enough to be simply anti-Zionist in orientation. It is past time that we consider the real, material steps that we must take to both sever the UC’s connections to Zionism and address the current and past harms created by those connections.

Dezionization entails not only ending the UC’s complicity in the genocidal actions of the Israeli state (which would include divestment and the end of formal research and teaching collaborations with Israeli-linked entities), but also confronting the role of Zionist organizations, donors, Regents, and administrators in repression targeted at members of the university community. title: [NYC] City workers push for full pension divestment from Israel after Comptroller caves on bonds (Chief-Leader)

A member of District Council 37 holds a sign imploring incoming Comptroller Mark Levine not to invest the city’s pension funds in Israeli stocks, bonds and companies last year.

Posted Friday, October 16, 2026 2:51 pm

City workers who pushed their unions to pass resolutions calling on the city’s pension fund to divest from Israeli stocks and bonds celebrated City Comptroller Mark Levine’s announcement on Wednesday that the city’s five pension funds would not be reinvesting in Israeli bonds. But the workers and pro-Palestinian advocates say they plan to continue pushing Levine to fully divest the over $200 million in investments the city’s five pension funds still hold in Israeli securities and companies.

“It feels like a victory initially,” said Tomasia Kastner, co-chair of City Workers for Palestine, a cross-union, cross-agency organizing group of pro-Palestinian workers who coordinate actions and strategy. “But when you look at the numbers, it no longer feels like a victory. It feels like a punch in the gut after a victory. It feels like one step forward two steps back.”

The pledge Levine made this week marked a reversal from the comptroller who promised on the campaign trail last year to reinvest in Israel after former Comptroller Brad Lander allowed $40 million of the pension system’s holdings in Israel to mature and expire.

title: Inside the fight to stop Israel-bound weapons at the East Coast’s biggest port (Mondoweiss)
content:
At Port Newark-Elizabeth, activists are escalating their tactics to stop weapons shipments to Israel. Mondoweiss reports from the port’s front lines.

By Joseph Mogul October 15, 20262

Activists with the Port of Elizabeth Movement block ZIM trucks carrying weapons components from entering the port on the morning of May 22, 2026. (Port of Elizabeth Movement)

A line of trucks rounded the bend toward Port Newark-Elizabeth on October 3, 2025. Inside the trailers were combat boots and weapons components — including 61 tons of forging rings used for military jets — bound for Israel via a Maersk vessel departing that morning.

But before the truckers could enter the port and the Maersk Sentosa could be loaded, 100 activists organized under the banner “Port of Elizabeth Movement” (POEM) sprang into action.

“It was ass o’clock in the morning. The sun was far from up. It was pitch black. Everyone was tired. Someone yelled, ‘Go, go, go, go!’” said Danny Creamer, who was later arrested at the POEM action.

Port Newark-Elizabeth is the third-largest port in the U.S. and the largest on the East Coast. And it has become a recurring target for activists concerned with the weapons supply chain to Israel. title: Universities fire dozens amid pressure from Zionist billionaires (Electronic Intifada)
content:
Ali Abunimah Rights and Accountability 14 October 2026

Universities in the United States and Canada have fired, suspended and harassed employees for speaking out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza, often using ostensibly neutral disciplinary procedures to conceal politically motivated retaliation.

That is the finding of a new report from the Academic Freedom Initiative, a project of the Middle East Studies Association (MESA).

“Lessons in Repression: Silencing Campus Workers on Palestine Since October 7, 2023” is the first systematic study of retaliation against university employees for their Palestine-related speech and activism in the two countries.

The report draws on a database of 196 incidents recorded through 20 August 2026 and in-depth interviews with 31 targeted employees.

Of those incidents, 76 – nearly 40 percent – resulted in termination, while 59 involved suspension or campus bans.

Both tenured professors and precariously employed instructors and staff have been targeted. Of 134 cases in which racial or ethnic identity was known, nearly two-thirds involved people of color. Some 16.5 percent of those targeted identified as Jewish.

Most retaliation had nothing to do with classroom teaching. More than half the incidents stemmed from other on-campus activities, including protests, while only 11 percent concerned alleged classroom interactions.

title: Trump Wanted Minnesota 15 Case to Be Another Prairieland. Instead, Twin Cities Rallied Behind Anti-ICE Activists. (The Intercept)
content:
The mainstream of Minnesota’s left-of-center politics — including unions, the backbone of Democratic power — are behind the radical left.

Demonstrators rally and march during an “ICE Out” day of protest on Jan. 23, 2026, in Minneapolis.Photo: Brandon Bell/Getty Images

As the Trump administration unveiled an indictment earlier this year against 15 anti-ICE activists, many of whom identify as radicals, for purportedly tormenting federal agents last winter, a top U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement official took the podium.

There were two types of protests, said Homeland Security Investigations special agent in charge Michael McCarthy, who oversaw the ICE agents in a St. Paul, Minnesota, field office who conducted the investigation.

“Peaceful protest is a protected right, and a cornerstone of our democracy,” said McCarthy. “When protest turns into rioting, violence or criminal activity, it becomes unlawful and it will not be tolerated.”

McCarthy’s comments stood in stark contrast with ICE’s record in Minneapolis, where a federal judge had been forced to issue an injunction to stop federal agents from pepper-spraying and arresting peaceful protesters during their enforcement blitz, dubbed Operation Metro Surge.

author: labor4pal
title: If They Can Criminalize the Minnesota 15, They Can Criminalize All of Us (Workers Resist)
content:
Against a backdrop of rising class struggle internationally — from Spain and France to Northern Ireland — the fight against the criminalization of anti-ICE activism, attacks on democratic rights, and union-busting has gained momentum over the past two weeks.

On October 3, nearly 500 people marched through downtown Minneapolis in support of the Minnesota 15 (MN15), political and union activists indicted by Donald Trump’s Justice Department for their organized opposition to the federal immigration crackdown in Minnesota known as Operation Metro Surge. That same day, solidarity events ranging from fundraising dinners to public meetings took place in 28 cities around the world, from New Haven, Connecticut, to Manchester, England.

The Minneapolis march drew broad support from the Minnesota labor movement, including the Minnesota AFL-CIO, Minnesota Nurses Association (MNA), Minneapolis Federation of Educators (MFE Local 59), Saint Paul Federation of Educators (SPFE Local 28), Minneapolis Regional Labor Federation, and eight other union locals.

This growing labor support reflects an understanding of what is at stake: the indictments of the MN15 are not simply an attack on 15 individuals. They are an attack on the ability of workers to organize collectively against government repression.

Evidence emerging from the MN15 discovery documents reinforces the seriousness of this threat.

title: Eyewitness report: Strikers and students rock France, Anti-fascism and Palestinian liberation mixed with anger at president Emmanuel Macron and the establishment (Socialist Worker-UK)
content:
Anti-fascism and Palestinian liberation mixed with anger at president Emmanuel Macron and the establishment

On the streets of Paris (Picture: Guy Smallman)

There were protests in 40 cities across France on Tuesday as workers and parents joined the movement of secondary school students demanding a future.

In Paris, organisers said 100,000 packed the streets. They were overwhelmingly young school and university students.

Young people chanted anti-fascist slogans. They included, “La jeunesse emmerde le Front National”—“The youth tell the Front National to fuck off” in a reference to the previous name of the fascist RN. And, “Siamo tutti antifascisti”—“We are all anti-fascist”.

They sang the Internationale and the French national anthem La Marseillaise. And there were Palestinian flags and chants of “free Palestine”. Other home made placards referenced the student and worker uprising of 1968.

When the presidential candidate for the left wing LFI party, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, arrived at the start of the march, he was mobbed by crowds of people. Both young and older protesters greeted him with chants of “president Mélenchon”.

Mélenchon called on his supporters, including many members of parliament, to join the protests. He wore a white armband on Tuesday to symbolise his support for the high school students.

title: The Case for Replacing UAW Monitor Neil Barofsky (UAWD Daily Struggle)
content:
Understanding Layoffs Fighting Layoffs Boom and Bust BlueOval Closure

Daily Struggle Editorial Board October 1, 2026

In 2024, UAW Monitor Neil Barofsky carried out an effort to intervene in UAW policy decisions and overturn the UAW’s opposition to the Israeli genocide in Gaza. Barofsky should be replaced for attacking the political independence of the UAW and violating his duties under the consent decree.

This is a republished UAWD resolution, with a new introduction to provide context, being co-released with The Struggle for Class-Independent Unionism in the Face of State Intervention.

Over the summer, the conflict between UAW President Shawn Fain and the UAW’s federal court-appointed monitor Neil Barofsky was back in the news. On June 25, Barofsky released his latest report alleging that Fain abused his authority and retaliated against the UAW’s Secretary-Treasurer Margaret Mock and Vice President Rich Boyer.

Fain countered the Monitor’s attack by saying Barfosky was “playing political games and abusing his power.” Specifically, the Monitor was punishing Fain for the UAW’s public position in favor of a ceasefire in Gaza.

author: labor4pal
title: Dockworkers Do Not Work For War — 30 October International Day of Action (No Harbour For Genocide et al)
content:
A post shared by No Harbour For Genocide (@noharbour4genocide)

On 30 October, dockworkers in more than 45 ports internationally will be take action against war and genocide.

Eight unions from France, Greece, Cyprus, the Basque Country, Türkiye, Morocco and Italy will refuse to let their ports be used to send weapons to war. They’re inviting port unions everywhere to join them.

They’re also taking action over their own working conditions. Dockworkers are being pushed into longer hours and seven-day weeks, secure jobs are being replaced with subcontracted and insecure work, and automation and AI are being used to cut jobs, all while pay falls further behind the cost of fuel, energy and food.

They’re asking for three things: no weapons or troops sent to war through their ports, no turning ports into military bases, and money spent on wages, safe jobs and pensions instead of weapons.

Save the date and share this post. Stay tuned, we’ll be sharing more on how ports work and how you can support the workers.

title: Over 200 organisations across more than 60 countries unite in Global Mobilisation for Palestine on 10 October (Middle East Monitor)
content:
LONDON — More than 200 civil society organisations, trade unions, student federations, human rights networks and grassroots groups across six continents will mobilise for Palestine on Saturday, 10 October, in a coordinated day of action spanning more than 60 countries.

Convened by the Global Alliance for Palestine, with the support of the Anti-Apartheid Movement (AAM) and the Global Coalition against Occupation of Palestine (SANED), this coordinated action seeks to create a unified, direct civil intervention intended to interrupt public complicity and demand systemic accountability against Israel’s war crimes and crimes against humanity. The Global Day of Action brings together markedly different forms of mobilisation under a shared international framework.

The scale of the mobilisation is reflected not only in the number of countries taking part, but in the variety of actions being organised. From major demonstrations in cities including London, Sydney/Warrane, Cape Town, São Paulo, Rabat, Quito, Mexico City, Istanbul, Santiago, Reykjavík and Bangkok, to blockades and interventions targeting government and commercial sites, multi-day cultural programmes, teach-ins, film screenings, vigils and student-led educational actions, the mobilisation will take markedly different forms across the countries taking part.

author: labor4pal
title: What is driving the shift on Palestine and war in the unions? (Socialist Worker-UK)
content:
In the run up to this year’s TUC conference, over 1,500 people signed a petition in support of the UCU motion asking the TUC to reaffirm its support for a position of “wages not weapons”

The TUC union federation conference this month carried motions that promoted a progressive position on war and Palestine.

The UCU union’s motion built upon last year’s “wages not weapons”, which officially ended the TUC’s policy of support for increasing arms spending.

This motion was opposed by only a handful of unions, albeit powerful ones such as Unite, GMB, Prospect and Community whose members work in defence.

On Palestine, TUC conference backed a motion brought by the AUE union that called to support the Palestinian-led Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement.

The motions carried reflect a significant shift that has taken place within the trade union movement.

TUC delegates are mainly made up of full-time officials not known for their radicalism. Days before the conference began TUC general secretary Paul Nowak launched an attack on the UCU motion.

He argued that “welfare not warfare” is a right wing slogan, arguing that the progressive position is welfare and warfare.

This was an attempt to shore up opposition to the motion to bring the TUC in line with the Labour government’s policy of increasing defence spending.
